title: Senior Director of Career and Professional Success
description:
Position Overview

The Senior Director of Career and Professional Success provides
strategic leadership for university-wide career readiness,
professional development, and postgraduate success. The position
advances proactive career mentoring, career education, and employer
engagement throughout the student experience. Through collaboration
with academic colleges, employers, alumni, and university partners,
the Senior Director expands access to meaningful career preparation
and supports successful transitions beyond Butler University.

Reporting to the Assistant Provost for Experiential Learning, this
position provides leadership and oversight for the Career and
Professional Success (CaPS) team, including five direct
reports.

Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership: Provide strategic leadership for Career
and Professional Success, advancing innovative, university-wide
approaches to career readiness, professional development, and
postgraduate success aligned with Butler University's mission and
priorities.
Career Mentoring: Oversee the implementation and multi-year
development of the Career Mentoring for All initiative, providing
strategic direction to the Associate Director of Career Mentoring
to ensure program quality, accessibility, sustainability, and
measurable student outcomes.
Academic Collaboration: Collaborate with academic deans,
faculty, and university leadership to develop college-specific
career preparation plans that integrate career exploration,
professional development, and experiential learning into students'
academic pathways.
Team Leadership: Lead and develop a high-performing Career and
Professional Success team, establishing clear expectations, shared
accountability, professional growth opportunities, and a culture of
innovation and continuous improvement.
Employer and Alumni Engagement: Develop strategic partnerships
with employers, alumni, and community organizations to expand
recruitment pipelines, professional networks, internships, co-ops,
and postgraduate employment opportunities.
Assessment and Outcomes: Establish and maintain an assessment
framework that evaluates career readiness, student engagement,
mentoring effectiveness, employer partnerships, and postgraduate
outcomes to inform continuous improvement and institutional
decision-making.
University-Wide Integration: Collaborate with university
partners to connect career development with academic advising,
experiential learning, undergraduate research, study away, public
service, and other educational experiences that advance student
success.
Operational Management: Direct Career and Professional Success
operations, including strategic planning, budgets, personnel,
technology, and resource allocation, while adapting services to
emerging workforce trends, technological advancements, and evolving
employer expectations.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in higher education, student affairs, human
resources, organizational leadership, business administration, or a
related field.
Minimum of seven years of progressively responsible experience
in career services, higher education administration, student
success, workforce development, talent development, employer
relations, or a related field.
Minimum of three years of leadership and supervisory
experience, including professional staff development,
organizational planning, and team leadership.
Demonstrated success leading strategic initiatives, managing
organizational change, and building collaborative partnerships
across diverse stakeholders.
Experience in budget management, resource allocation, program
assessment, and data-informed decision-making.
Knowledge of career development practices, workforce trends,
employer recruiting strategies, experiential learning, and
postgraduate career preparation.
Excellent communication, interpersonal, and organizational
skills, with demonstrated ability to influence stakeholders, build
consensus, and collaborate across organizational
boundaries.

Preferred Qualifications

Master's degree in higher education, student affairs, business
administration, organizational leadership, or a related field.
Demonstrated experience leading university-wide career
development or student success initiatives involving multiple
academic colleges or departments.
Experience implementing, expanding, or overseeing career
mentoring programs, employer engagement strategies, or
institution-wide career readiness initiatives.
Experience establishing assessment frameworks and using student
engagement, career readiness, and postgraduate outcomes data to
inform institutional strategy.
Demonstrated success cultivating and maintaining relationships
with alumni in key industries, connecting current students with
alumni professionals, and leading teams in strategic alumni
outreach to expand career mentoring, internship, and employment
opportunities for students.

About Us

Butler University is a private, nationally recognized comprehensive
university encompassing seven colleges: Arts, Business,
Communication, Education, Liberal Arts & Sciences, Pharmacy
& Health Sciences and Founder's College. Approximately 4,500
undergraduate and 1,000 graduate and doctoral students are enrolled
at Butler, representing 46 states and 24 countries.

Join us at the crossroads of tradition & transformation. A
career at Butler University offers more than just a job—it’s an
opportunity to join a dedicated, innovative, and supportive
community grounded in equity, academic excellence, and meaningful
impact. Aligned with Boldly Butler, our strategic plan, faculty and
staff play a vital role in delivering transformational learning
experiences, enriching our campus and community, and ensuring a
thriving Butler for generations to come.

Butler University is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome
applications from all individuals, regardless of age, sex, race,
religion, color, disability, protected veteran status, national
origin, or any other legally protected category.
